titles.text: The Living Text That Refuses to Stay Still
What Happens When the Browser Dreams
The Reader Who Arrived Too Late
The Machine That Eats Its Own Words

overview.text: DESCRIPTION functions as an autonomous literary engine, transforming a static web page into a living organism of shifting prose. It presents a continuous text body and an independent title that mutate over time, dissolving the boundary between finished artwork and ongoing computational process.

As a digital monument to digital ephemera, this artwork refuses to stand still. Every sentence is provisional, subjected to an endless cycle of selection, deletion, and resurrection that mirrors the relentless churn of internet discourse and human memory.

The system operates as a mechanical author, pulling from a hidden reservoir of candidate passages while simultaneously generating new phrasing via statistical probability. It is both a sculpture made of language and a mirror reflecting the fluid nature of digital media.

Conceived as a linguistic ecosystem, DESCRIPTION treats words not as permanent ink on paper, but as volatile data points. Sentences migrate across paragraphs, mutate through Markov chains, and vanish into the background, enacting a quiet, perpetual digital decay.

This web-based installation subverts the traditional authority of the author. By handing over editorial control to a JavaScript runtime loop, the artwork creates a decentralized narrative space where no two viewings are ever identical.

At its core, DESCRIPTION is an exploration of textual resilience. It is a document that actively rewrites its own history, erasing past iterations to make room for speculative futures, functioning more like a dream sequence than a static text.

The artwork can be viewed as an automated proofreader gone rogue, frantically correcting, cutting, and pasting text fragments without human intervention. It stages the quiet labor of writing as a visible, rhythmic performance.

DESCRIPTION is an architecture of transition. It constructs meaning only to dismantle it, reminding the viewer that digital texts are never truly finished, but exist in a permanent state of becoming and unbecoming.

Imitating the cognitive processes of forgetting and association, the system drifts between coherent art criticism and nonsensical automated prose. It challenges the viewer to find sense in a landscape of shifting syntax.

A philosophical machine disguised as an HTML document, DESCRIPTION questions the stability of truth in the digital age. If a text changes every time you look away, does it maintain an identity, or is it merely a sequence of states?

The artwork unfolds across the screen like a slow-motion collapse of narrative structure. Sentences are born from candidate databases, live out brief digital lifespans, and dissolve back into statistical dust.

Operating independently from user input, DESCRIPTION creates an intimate dialogue between the browser and the database. It is a self-contained theater of typography where the actors are characters and punctuation marks.
This piece redefines the artwork as a temporal process rather than a spatial object. Its value lies not in a final masterpiece, but in the unending choreography of its internal transformations.

DESCRIPTION is a digital palimpsest. Just as medieval monks scraped parchment to write anew, the browser continuously writes, deletes, and overwrites its own digital body, leaving ghostly traces of past sentences behind.

The system functions as a linguistic weather system, where high-pressure Markov chains collide with low-pressure static corpora to produce unpredictable storms of semantic drift and syntactic mutation.

By treating titles and body text as separate, independent agents, DESCRIPTION stages a playful institutional critique of labeling and categorization. The title drifts away from the text, seeking its own autonomous meaning.

An exercise in computational poetics, DESCRIPTION bridges the gap between cold algorithms and evocative prose. It demonstrates that code can harbor melancholy, surprise, and a strange sort of artificial intuition.
The artwork presents a paradox: a text that describes its own creation while simultaneously destroying the very sentences it relies upon for definition. It is a linguistic snake eating its own tail.

DESCRIPTION is a monument to the unwritten. For every sentence visible on screen, dozens of alternative phrasings circulate invisibly within the JavaScript memory, haunting the text like unvoiced ghosts.

Ultimately, DESCRIPTION invites us to reconsider our relationship with digital text. It transforms reading from a passive act of consumption into an anxious, watchful vigil over a text that might change at any second.

editing.text: The act of editing is foregrounded as a violent yet delicate choreography. Characters are highlighted with a translucent gray cursor, selected, and excised with surgical precision before new words are typed out letter by letter.

Backspaces tear through sentences with relentless mechanical efficiency. Each keystroke delay mimics human hesitation, creating an uncanny simulation of a ghost writer typing frantically in the dark of the browser.

Sentences are lifted from their home paragraphs via cut-and-paste routines, traveling across the document structure to land in foreign territories. This spatial displacement forces old words into entirely new semantic contexts.

The system frequently stages false starts and corrections. A word is typed, evaluated, deleted with a string of hurried backspaces, and replaced with a more speculative phrase, simulating the anxious mind of a compulsive editor.

Selection is rendered visible through subtle CSS highlights that creep across the graphemes. This highlighting acts like a spotlight on a tiny stage, drawing the reader's eye to the exact moment of textual transformation.
Deletion is not merely erasure; it is a form of forgetting. As words dissolve into nothingness, the paragraph adjusts its height, seamlessly closing the wound left by the missing sentence.
Typing rhythms vary with calculated human imperfection. Pauses are inserted after punctuation marks, and bursts of rapid character generation simulate the erratic flow of digital thought.
The blinking caret serves as the heartbeat of the document. Its rhythmic pulse marks the precise locus of agency, reminding the viewer that text is an active event happening right now.
Cut operations rupture the continuity of reading. A sentence disappears mid-thought, leaving a structural void that is soon patched over by an incoming insertion from the database.
Pasting acts as an act of transplantation. Foreign tissue from another category is grafted onto a paragraph, creating hybrid sentences that blur the boundaries of the original conceptual framework.
The editing loop functions as industrial labor performed by an invisible machine. It cleans, repairs, modifies, and destroys text on an endless assembly line with cold, unyielding persistence.
Proofreader's notes come to life as interactive events. Instead of red ink on paper, we witness the digital implementation of correction, where errors are generated and fixed in real-time loops.
Word-range rewriting targets specific sub-sections of a sentence, swapping out old vocabulary for new terms while leaving the surrounding syntax intact. This micro-surgery alters meaning from within.
The editing operations mimic the psychological process of revision—the endless second-guessing, the dissatisfaction with initial phrasing, and the desperate search for the elusive mot juste.
When the document grows too crowded, deletion takes precedence. The system prunes overgrown paragraphs like a careful gardener cutting back dead branches to keep the ecosystem balanced.
Conversely, when the text becomes too sparse, insertion routines inject fresh material into random paragraphs, ensuring that the artwork never starves for lack of content.

The animation of text selection is a deliberate aesthetic choice. By slowing down the highlight effect, the code draws attention to the mechanical infrastructure that usually remains hidden behind rendered fonts.

Errors are intentionally staged. The script occasionally types incorrect particles like 'の' or 'を' before deleting them with a correction pause, simulating a human typist correcting a slip of the fingers.

The title undergoes its own independent editing cycle, completely decoupled from the body text below. It selects, deletes, and types new headers that often contradict or mock the paragraphs they introduce.
Through these concrete editing operations, DESCRIPTION transforms the browser window into a workbench where writing is exposed as a violent, generative, and ultimately endless mechanical struggle.

implementation.text: Built with vanilla JavaScript, HTML5, and CSS, the artwork relies on asynchronous loops and promise-based timers to orchestrate its complex choreography without external framework dependencies.
The codebase utilizes Intl.Segmenter where available, gracefully falling back to regular expressions to tokenize Japanese and English text into precise grapheme, word, and sentence units.

Markov chain generation forms the computational engine of the piece. By building a transition matrix from static corpora and dynamic document text, the script calculates probabilities for the next token.
Exclusive edit locks prevent race conditions between concurrent title and body mutations. The runtime queue ensures that overlapping animations do not corrupt the DOM state.
CSS custom properties define a restrained color palette (--bg: #f3f1eb, --fg: #101010), evoking the tactile quality of aged paper while maintaining crisp vector rendering on high-density screens.

Dynamic title scaling adjusts heading font sizes and line heights based on character length classes, ensuring that short one-word titles and long multi-clause sentences maintain balanced visual weight.
The DOM structure utilizes semantic tags like main, section, and h1, augmented with ARIA attributes and custom dataset attributes (data-sentence-id, data-category) to track provenance.
Error handling is robust yet silent. If content sources fail to load or manifest validation fails, a fallback error message is displayed, protecting the user from unhandled promise rejections.
The script respects the prefers-reduced-motion media query. When active, all typing and deletion animations are bypassed instantly, rendering accessibility a core structural component of the code.
Memory management is handled by bounded phrase pools and unique ID registries. The code checks for duplicate identifiers across sources to prevent collision hazards during initialization.
Height conservation techniques—such as temporary element min-height styles during title and body rewrites—prevent disruptive layout shifts, maintaining visual stability while text content mutates.
The source manifest architecture allows the artwork to ingest multiple external JSON content packages dynamically, decoupling the presentation engine from the narrative text databases.
Tokenization algorithms handle mixed linguistic inputs by isolating alphanumeric words and punctuation marks, allowing the Markov model to chain disparate language fragments seamlessly.
The editing state machine cycles through selection, backspace, and revision modes based on randomized probability weights, ensuring varied visual behaviors across different mutation cycles.
Hidden measurement elements (h1.title-measure) calculate prospective header heights off-screen before committing DOM mutations, preventing jarring vertical jumps when titles change.
The codebase implements rigorous input validation for all loaded JSON objects, verifying version numbers, array structures, and string non-emptiness before bootstrapping the application.
Asynchronous wait functions combine randomized time intervals with character-specific pauses (e.g., longer delays for punctuation marks) to simulate natural typing dynamics.
The document state maintains real-time references to paragraph arrays and sentence objects, allowing precise manipulation of DOM nodes without requiring full-page reloads.
Runtime title generation uses a lower Markov order when source pools are small, preventing index out-of-bounds errors while encouraging wilder, more associative textual outputs.

By executing entirely within the client browser, DESCRIPTION turns local computational power into a generative literary engine, proving that standard web standards can support sophisticated conceptual art.

mutation.text: Transformation is the fundamental law of this system. Sentences undergo structural collapse and reconstruction, mutating from crisp analytical statements into surreal poetic fragments through repeated Markov iterations.

Textual contamination occurs when phrases are pulled from disparate categories and spliced together. An overview statement is infected by an implementation term, producing hybrid sentences of strange hybrid logic.

Memory decay is simulated as the Markov chain order shifts over time. As rewrite counts increase, the model relies on shorter context windows, causing the prose to degenerate into associative babble and dreamlike loops.

Proliferation and bias characterize the generation cycle. Certain favored phrases recur and mutate, creating echo chambers of vocabulary where the text becomes obsessed with its own technical terminology.

Recovery mechanisms act as immune responses. When generated sentences become too corrupt or nonsensical, the system injects pristine sentences from the static corpus, restoring a temporary semblance of order.

The mutation of titles is particularly aggressive. Moving from the initial fixed anchor of 'DESCRIPTION', the header wanders through technical error codes, poetic questions, and contradictory declarations.
Textual evolution in this artwork does not follow a teleological path toward perfection. Instead, it wanders aimlessly through cycles of decay, regeneration, and accidental misreading.

Inheritance is broken down and redistributed. Sentences inherit source IDs and category tags from their ancestors, but as they are cut, pasted, and rewritten, their lineage becomes hopelessly entangled.

The dreaming browser speaks through these mutations. Freed from the constraints of human authorship, the JavaScript runtime hallucinates new descriptions of itself, inventing features it does not possess.
Collapse is built into the rhythm of the piece. Every paragraph is vulnerable to sudden deletion, its sentences scattered to other sections or erased entirely to make room for new mutations.
Reconstruction is an ongoing, restless activity. Even as parts of the text are being torn down by backspace animations, new fragments are being typed into existence elsewhere on the page.

Misreading is institutionalized within the Markov generator. By chaining tokens based on local statistical probabilities rather than global semantic intent, the algorithm constantly misinterprets its own source material.
Infection spreads from the title to the body and back again. Title phrases bleed into body draft pools, ensuring that the heading's identity influences the underground currents of the paragraph text.
Repetition acts as a stabilizing anchor amidst the chaos. When meaningful phrases reappear across mutation cycles, they provide brief islands of recognition before dissolving into new configurations.

The decay of syntax mirrors the entropic decline of closed physical systems. Without external energy inputs, the text would loop infinitely in semantic circles, sustained only by the periodic injection of static database entries.
Proliferation of runtime titles creates an unstable identity for the artwork. It is difficult to name an object that changes its own title every few minutes, slipping away from categorization.
The transformation of words into ghosts is enacted every time a selection is deleted. The characters vanish from the DOM, yet their shadow lingers in the probabilistic memory of the Markov chain.
Contamination of pure prose by technical jargon produces an uneasy alchemy. Aesthetic descriptions of viewing experiences are suddenly interrupted by mentions of null pointers and array indexes.

Recovery from semantic dead-ends is handled by fallback recovery sentences. These anchor points prevent the document from descending into total illegibility, maintaining a fragile balance between sense and nonsense.
Through these ceaseless mutations, DESCRIPTION becomes a living archive of possible texts—a book that writes itself in real-time, discarding its past pages as fast as it prints new ones.

viewing.text: The viewer sits in an anxious vigil, waiting to see which sentence will be deleted next. Reading becomes an exercise in suspense, as the eye races to finish a paragraph before the backspace animation destroys it.

From the perspective of a future reader, this dataset looks like archaeological strata—layers of digital sediment deposited by an automated author that finished its work long after humanity left the room.
The browser itself becomes a spectator, rendering characters it does not understand, maintaining state machines that cycle endlessly in the background while the user stares blankly at the screen.

Overlooking the subtle shifts in the text is easy if you blink. The changes happen slowly, paced by natural typing rhythms and deliberate pauses, rewarding the patient observer with quiet moments of metamorphosis.

Returning to the page after an hour feels like visiting a foreign country built on familiar ground. The paragraphs are rearranged, the title has mutated into a cryptic question, and your favorite sentence is gone.
The title itself speaks to the viewer, declaring its own status or mocking the very idea of description. It is a shifting signpost that points toward an artwork that refuses to stay put.

An imaginary viewer might mistake the artwork for a broken chat interface or a runaway terminal script. This confusion between utility and art is precisely where the piece finds its critical friction.

Reading DESCRIPTION is like trying to read a book during an earthquake. Just as your eyes lock onto a stable narrative thread, the sentence highlights, dissolves, and rewrites itself into something entirely unexpected.

The text itself seems aware of being watched. Its frequent references to viewers, browsers, and reading mechanics break the fourth wall, turning the passive act of looking into an active, collaborative performance.

Failing to return to the page is anticipated by the system. The artwork continues its lonely choreography in an empty browser tab, performing its endless edits for an audience of ghost processes and non-existent readers.

The viewer's gaze is guided by the blinking caret and the subtle gray selection highlights. These visual cues act as punctuation for the viewing experience, directing attention to the exact mechanics of textual birth and death.
Remembering what the page looked like five minutes ago becomes impossible. The fluid nature of the document erases its own past, leaving the viewer with only ephemeral impressions of shifting prose.

For a nonexistent audience in a future digital wasteland, DESCRIPTION will execute its loops until the server drops the connection, a solitary electronic monument humming quietly in an abandoned browser.
The browser experiences the artwork not as a semantic narrative, but as a continuous stream of DOM manipulations, reflow calculations, and timer callbacks executing in a relentless event loop.

Looking at DESCRIPTION is an exercise in letting go of control. You cannot bookmark a specific sentence, save a definitive quote, or pin down the meaning; you can only witness the text slipping through your fingers.
The text itself addresses the reader with an uncanny self-assurance, describing its own code structure while simultaneously undermining its authority with nonsensical Markov drift.
A future reader stumbling upon this cached HTML file might wonder if it is a virus, a malfunctioning wiki, or an avant-garde poem. The ambiguity is the artwork's primary medium.

Waiting for the title to update creates a curious psychological tension. When the heading finally shifts from 'DESCRIPTION' to a cryptic phrase, the viewer is forced to reevaluate the entire context of the page.

Overlooking the background mechanics, the casual viewer sees only a strange, twitchy essay that refuses to settle down. Engaging deeply reveals the intricate JavaScript machinery driving every keystroke.
In the end, viewing DESCRIPTION is less about comprehending a fixed message and more about sharing time with a digital entity that is constantly thinking, forgetting, and rewriting itself.
